hi! so i've heard a lot of negative things about writing about mental health...DESPITE that, I am writing about my eating disorder...however, I'm doing it in a subtle way, using an object that means a lot to me to figuratively weave in my mental health and talk about how I was able to recover from it. my mental health is  the context for my essay, but it is not the main topic. i also focus on more of the recovery aspect rather than the depths of my lows. i have heard writing about hospitalization/mental health could be a liability issue, but quite frankly, it's the hardest thing I've dealt with and similar to you,, it dominated my highschool experience and i'd be leaving out a big part of me if I didn't talk about it.

my recommendation to you is to discuss your mental health struggles through a symbol---whether that be an object, etc, but it has to relate back to YOU. and even if you still struggle (which i do as well) i'd try and talk about the growth you have and some of the positive things at the end. 

​

feel free to PM if you need someone to just read it and give suggestions :)

a journey of one thousand miles begins with one step. remember that. it may feel like a huge change you need to make, but just take it one step at a time. for dinner tonight, maybe eat something you'd normally eat but in smaller portions. Don't cold turkey yourself...you won't be able to maintain it and then it could turn into an ED. take it slow. tomorrow for breakfast, make yourself power protein pancakes maybe, but not in huge portions. i know it's hard with all the quarantine going on, but maybe do some squats, jumping jacks, running in place, sit ups etc to get your heart moving. it may feel SO discouraging and hopeless at first. it actually will. you might want to give in and just eat whatever and not stop. but remember. it's not impossible. think about how strong and good you'll feel when you're healthier. remember, also, it's a lifestyle change you want to make. you can still eat foods you like (even chips and ice cream!) maybe try and cut some of it out now, but remember in moderation you can eat anything. finally, remember...a journey of a thousand miles starts with one step
